messages:
rachel: Quick heads-up: a user hit runtime errors when importing our JS SDK in an Edge function. Error: 'require is not defined' and stack pointing to dist/cjs/index.js. They deployed on Cloudflare Pages with Worker runtime.

devish: ugh. Our publish currently sets main -> dist/cjs, module -> dist/esm, and no conditional exports. Workers will try to load main when tools don't honor module.

jon: yep. Modern approach is conditional exports in package.json. Something like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "worker": "./dist/esm/worker-entry.js"
  }
}
```

priya: we've talked about adding a worker condition. Node and bundlers usually ignore it, but Deno/Cloudflare can pick it up. But many tools don't know "worker" condition unless we document it.

rachel: also typing oddities: VSCode sometimes resolves to the CJS typings which change shape (module.exports style) and intellisense breaks. We might need a "typesVersions" map for TS consumers on older TS versions.

devish: alternative is two packages: @redwood/inference and @redwood/inference-compat. Keep compat as CJS-first for older infra. Pros: avoids weird resolver edge cases. Cons: splits install surface and support.

jon: I prefer single package with explicit export conditions + clear README. We can provide a small compatibility shim package that re-exports the main package for older node versions instead of full split. Much easier to maintain.

priya: build/tooling work: need a separate ES module build targeted for workers (no node:fs, no process usage). tsup supports multiple targets but we must ensure tree-shaking removes polyfills. Also ensure package-lock doesn't pull node polyfills via older bundlers.

rachel: sample app fix: quickstarts currently show CommonJS examples: `const Redwood = require('redwood-inference')`. We should swap to ESM examples and add a Worker quickstart: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and show how to configure env via Cloudflare secrets or Vercel env.

mark: ci-bot: queued job smoketest/canary-edge for 0.13.0-canary.2. Includes Node16, Node18, Bun, Cloudflare Workers emulator, and a Next Edge sample.

devish: typing distribution: emit a flat dist/index.d.ts and also per-subpath declarations under dist/esm/*.d.ts and dist/cjs/*.d.ts. Then export types in package.json top-level "types" and mirror inside exports to be safe. Some editors prefer explicit subpath types.

jon: small gotcha: consumers using `const sdk = require('redwood-inference')` will get module.exports shape. To avoid ESM default confusion we should ensure CJS entry does `module.exports = require('../esm/index.js')` or create a CJS wrapper that sets `exports.default = module.exports`. Keep shape identical.

priya: runtime checks: detect environment at build time and remove any process.env references in the runtime bundle, or gate them behind inlined replacements. Otherwise workers fail because process is undefined.

rachel: onboarding docs: add a quick checkbox near SDK download: "Target runtime: Node | Bun | Edge | Deno" and show a one-liner install + import sample for each. That would cut down support tickets.

mark: ci-bot: smoke tests scheduled. Will post results in this thread when done.

devish: plan proposal in short: 1) single package with conditional exports (import/require/worker/default), 2) produce ESM worker-targeted build without node shims, 3) emit comprehensive d.ts + types mapping, 4) update quickstarts to ESM + Worker examples, 5) add CI smoke tests for Edge.

jon: +1. If we hit resolver regressions for customers using old bundlers, we'll publish the -compat package as stopgap. But let's try single-package first.

priya: I'll start the tsup config PR for dual outputs and a small example for Cloudflare Pages.

rachel: thanks. I'll update the onboarding checklist and coordinate with docs to swap the CJS snippets.

mark: ci-bot: canary tests passed on Node16/18 and Next Edge sample failed due to missing export for worker condition. See logs: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module './dist/esm/worker-entry.js'`.

devish: ok that explains current user issue. I'll patch the build to emit worker-entry.js and push another canary.

rachel: awesome. keep this thread for follow-ups, and please ping if anyone wants pair review on package.json exports mapping.
